messages.subject: [statnet_help] Meta-analysis for ERGM
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,I have a question about the ERGM. 
I'm trying to fit an ERGM on a large social network dataset, containing 20 different classes (about 1200 actors). I've fit the model in classes separately. After that I want to join these results into a single one . I wonder if there are any tools or codes for meta-analysis about ERGM ?
I hope you understand my question. 
Many thanks, 

Xu Gangmin Shanghai normal University

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Meta-analysis for ERGM
messages.body_plain:
If you would like to pool your results from 20 different (i.e., 
completely independent) networks with approximately the same 
data-generating process in one single model, you could use a TERGM 
without any temporal dependency terms. For example, the btergm function 
in the btergm package could be used to do this. Some documentation can 
be found here: http://www.philipleifeld.com/cms/upload/btergm.pdf

Best,

Philip

--

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Meta-analysis for ERGM
messages.body_plain:
Hej Xu Gangmin,

Philip's suggestion is a good one. Alternatively, it is easy to extract 
ergm-results from your classwise estimation and aggregate results with a 
meta-analysis software. Here what Weihua An (2015) recommends:
> These estimation methods have been detailed in prior literature 
> (e.g.,White, 2011; Gasparrini et al., 2012) and implemented in 
> statisti-cal packages such as ?metafor? (Viechtbauer, 2010) and 
> ?mvmeta?(Gasparrini et al., 2012) in R and ?mvmeta? in Stata (White, 
> 2011).
An, Weihua (2015): Multilevel meta network analysis with application to 
studying network dynamics of network interventions. Social Networks 43 
(2015) 48?56.
Gasparrini, A., Armstrong, B., Kenward, M.G., 2012. Multivariate 
meta-analysis for non-linear and other multi-parameter associations. 
Stat. Med. 31 (29),3821?3839.
Viechtbauer, W., 2010. Conducting meta-analyses in R with the metafor 
package. J.Stat. Softw. 36 (3), 1?48.
White, I.R., 2011. Multivariate random-effects meta-regression: updates 
to mvmeta.Stata J. 11 (2), 255?270.

And let me add, as Philip suggested as much, and as there is a certain 
body of applications suggesting as much: ERGM estimates are only under 
strong assumptions (process has reached equilibrium, all confounding 
processes were observed and are included in the model specification) 
useful for conclusions about data-generating processes. It is a bit 
unfortunate that such process interpretation suggestions in the 
literature often do not properly spell out the assumptions required for 
making them.

All the best, Christian

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Predicting changes in node network centrality over time
messages.body_plain:
Hello

I have a complete adjacency matrix for 9 time points. I also have node
attribute data collected only at the first time point. Is there a way to
use statnet (or any other program) to estimate the effect of node attribute
data on node network centrality over time?

My first impulse is to calculate the network centrality statistics for each
node at each time point. Then use the network centrality values as outcome
variables in a regular time series analysis with node attributes as the
predictor variable. But network centrality scores seem to violate data
independence assumptions. Is there a way to estimate node effects on
centrality over time?

Thanks for any help

Chris Carpenter

messages.body_plain:
Dear Chris CarpenterFirst let me ask you a question. Is your network "stochastic actor oriented"? Simply I mean, do the actors of the network decide to change their network, and is the network changing over time? If yes, I think I have an answer for your question. Here is my thought:If I were you, I would use RSiena tool to model the evolution of the network over time. In this case, your dependent variable would be "creating or maintaining a tie" , which would reflect centrality. You can estimate the effect of actors' attributes as well as structural features on your dependent variable.?I hope it helps and let me know if you have more question. Please apologize me if you already thought about this solution.?Best Regards?Saeede Eftekhari

messages.body_plain:
No problem. You are right. Rsiena is used mainly for formation. But Rsiena is the only method that i know for modeling longitudinal data! 

Does time really matter for you? I am asking this as you do not have changing covariate ( you said you have feature only in first time point).
So, actually, i am not sure if you really need using panel data to model the evolution in order to find the impact of features. Is my point clear?

I would suggest simplu define you dependent variables and use QAP regressions. Then, use the other points of data for robustness check. It may look simple, but i think at least you can see if there is any impact.
I hope it helps. Let me know if you have any thoughts.

messages.body_plain:
Hi, Chris.  If your nodal attributes are constant, then what do you mean 
by their having an effect on centrality over time?  This can be made 
meaningful, but only in the context of a more specific class of 
assumptions.  (For instance, if you posited a growth model for 
centrality whose parameter was putatively related to the covariate, you 
could test that.)

Without such additional clarifications, your problem is ill-posed: you 
are asking for the relationship between a vector of real numbers and a 
vector of time series.  (In this case, the fact that your time series 
come from a network is a red herring.)  There are many kinds of 
relationships that one could seek, but you will need to be more specific 
about what you want to know in order for us to be of much help...

-Carter

TERGMs (with e.g. STERGMs as an important special case), dynamic latent 
variable models (e.g., dynamic latent space models, DRIFT, etc.), REMs, 
etc. would all be examples of non-SAB families for longitudinal 
relational data.  If one is interested in exploratory analysis (rather 
than modeling per se), one could add time series analysis of network 
descriptives, multidimensional scaling of Hamming or structural 
distances, etc.  There are quite a lot of alternatives, whose 
applicability depends on what you are willing to assume, and what you 
want to achieve.

messages.subject: [statnet_help] STERGM on valued networks?
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

Does anyone have advice on how to use a STERGM on a valued network? I'm
following along with the Sunbelt 2015 PDF by Krivitsky and Butts (
https://statnet.org/trac/raw-attachment/wiki/Sunbelt2015/Valued.pdf) on how
to run an ERGM on a valued network, and I can replicate with my own
networks, but when I attempt to create a STERGM I keep hitting an error
dialogue:

"Error in locate.InitFunction(term, paste0(termroot, "Term"), "ERGM term")
:
  ERGM term ?sum? initialization function ?InitErgmTerm.sum? not found."

I'm far from a final set of coefficients, but in my attempts to see if I
can run a STERGM on the valued network snapshots, the "model" below works
as one would expect, while "temporal_model" always hits that error. I'm
very new to ERGMs so it's entirely plausible this is user error due to
ignorance or failure to find the right Google query that addresses this
question, but I've been unable to find a definitive answer to this question.

Models I'm running:

samp <- list()
samp[[1]] <- get_graph_weighted("timestep_1.gml")
samp[[2]] <- get_graph_weighted("timestep_2.gml")
samp[[3]] <- get_graph_weighted("timestep_3.gml")
samp[[4]] <- get_graph_weighted("timestep_4.gml")
samp[[5]] <- get_graph_weighted("timestep_5.gml")
model <-
ergm(samp[[1]]~sum+mutual+edges+absdiff("political")+absdiff("defaultstatus")+nodeicov("trafficcount")+nodeocov("trafficcount"),
response = "observed",reference = ~Poisson)
temporal_model <- stergm(samp,
  response = "observed",
  reference = ~Poisson,
  formation=
~sum+mutual+edges+absdiff("political")+absdiff("defaultstatus")+nodeicov("trafficcount")+nodeocov("trafficcount"),
  dissolution =
~sum+mutual+edges+absdiff("political")+absdiff("defaultstatus")+nodeicov("trafficcount")+nodeocov("trafficcount"),
  estimate = "CMLE",
  times=1:5
)

Each GML is read in igraph, converted via intergraph, then igraph is
detached and we proceed as normal with statnet.


Best,
Devin Gaffney
Northeastern University

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Question about directed shared partner terms
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Question about directed shared partner terms
messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet team,

I apologize in advance for the long intro. I thought it was important to 
give some background to what I am trying to do.

*Intro:*

I have been 'playing around' a lot with the statnet ergm package 
recently. What I am currently interested in is to explore the 
possibility of applying erg modeling to event graphs. That is, directed 
graphs where the nodes are events, and where the edges (in my case) 
indicate which events (tails) occurred in response to which other events 
(heads). I have been using the idea of representing social processes as 
event graphs for a while now, but I have never been able to really go 
beyond using this as a visual aid in a largely qualitative, interpretive 
analysis. I hope that ergms of event graphs can help me get more out of 
this approach. Just as a note on the side, I am also aware of, and 
exploring other approaches to studying social dynamics, including 
relational event models and stochastic actor-oriented models (especially 
those adapted for events [e.g., Stadtfeld's work]), but I am very keen 
to explore the idea of 'social processes as event graphs' as well, 
because I think it could lead to complementary insights. I am also aware 
that the interpretation of the modeling terms, and of the models 
themselves changes by applying ergms to event graphs. One thing that I 
am doing is thinking about the meaning of statistics like ostars, 
twopaths, transitive triads, shared partners, nodemix, nodematch and so 
on in the context of event graphs.

An important difference between the event graphs that I am trying to 
model, and the social network graphs that ergms are usually applied to, 
is that the nodes in event graphs are ordered in time. That is, edges 
can only point from nodes (events) that occur later in time, to nodes 
(events) that occur earlier in time. This also means that edges can, for 
example, never be reciprocal, and that only a limited number of 
triangles can exist (transitive triangles can occur, but cycles cannot). 
So basically, I am working with Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), although 
the acyclic nature of the graphs is a consequence of the chronological 
order of the nodes, rather than being at defining feature of event 
graphs. Simply put, all edges in event graphs obey the rule that an edge 
i->j cannot exist if i happened before j. The random graphs that are 
considered by the ergm package (under normal circumstances) of course do 
not obey this rule. To impose this rule on my models, I use the 
ergm-constraints function. I wrote a simple script for R that steps 
through all the dyads in a network, and if the dyad breaks the rule, it 
puts a 1 in a new adjacency matrix for the corresponding dyad. I then 
turn this adjacency matrix into a network object, and then tell the 
ergm-constraints function to keep all the edges in this network fixed as 
absent. This seems to work, at least to some extent, because all 
simulations of models that I created with this constraint obey the 
appropriate rule (edges never point forward in time).

*My puzzle:*

However, *and here comes my question/puzzle*, I was wondering if this 
rule also appropriately translates into the way that statistics are 
calculated. It seems to do so for the edges term. If I translate the 
coefficient for the edges term to a probability, it gives me a measure 
of density that respects the fact that certain edges can never occur. 
However, I was unsure whether the rule is also respected when I look at 
statistics like dyad-wise shared partners. If I understand it right, the 
gw versions of shared partner statistics also consider the number of 
dyads for which the number of shared partners is 0. When counting the 
number of dyads for which this is true, does the algorithm respect the 
fact that certain dyads should be excluded from the count? In other 
words, is it enough to include the constraints that I discuss in the 
intro above, or should I also consider developing adapted versions of 
some of the statistics? (I am not that experienced in statistical 
modeling, but I am fairly experienced in programming in C++, which is 
very similar to C).

*Another, related point:
*While looking into the characteristics of the various terms for shared 
partner distributions, I also encountered something I did not fully 
understand. I saw that there are directed version for the shared partner 
distributions (e.g., desp, ddsp, dgwesp, and so on), which are very 
interesting to me because of their potential meaning in the context of 
event graphs. I also understood (correct me if I am wrong) that, for 
directed networks, the esp.OTP term should essentially be the same as 
the original esp term (OTP is the default choice). However, the 
summaries for these statistics seem to be different.

Consider the following example. I created a simple network of 4 nodes 
and 4 directed edges (see attached file): A->B, A->C, B->D, C->D. If I 
load this network into R, I get the following results if I study their 
dyadwise shared partner distributions:

 > summary(net~dsp(0:3))
dsp0 	dsp1
	dsp2
	dsp3
11
	0
	1
	0


 > summary(net~ddsp(0:3, type = 'OTP'))
dsp0 	dsp1
	dsp2
	dsp3
-1
	0
	1
	0


I have the impression that something goes wrong here. Is it a mistake on 
my side?

Unfortunately, I am not that experienced in statistical modeling, 
although I am very keen to learn more about it, and I am currently 
investing a lot of time and energy in that. However, there are still 
plenty of things that are hard for me to get my head around. I really 
appreciate any help.

Apologies again for the long email. And many thanks for your time and 
patience if you have gotten this far. :)

With kind regards,

Wouter

messages.subject: [statnet_help] STERGM on valued networks?
messages.body_plain:
Hello, Devin,

Good question! STERGMs were developed for binary networks and use some
properties fundamental to them. Extending the framework to valued
networks is subject for ongoing research.

At this point, you can use the previous time step's network as, say a
dyadic covariate to estimate parameters for one transition. You'll need
to do it manually, unfortunately.

						Best,
						Pavel
